## Purpose
The main authenticated dashboard page (`/dashboard`) — the app's central client component, owning auth/session bootstrap, chat state, per-section preview content, the live run's WebSocket/SSE connection, and dispatch of incoming stream events into the various preview/chat/history surfaces.

## Shape
- `DashboardPage` — the default-exported page component; holds a large set of `useState`/`useRef` slots for auth (`token`, `user`), chat (`messages`, `activeChatId`, streaming buffers), per-workflow-type preview content (`userStoryContent`, `pptContent`, `prototypeContent`, `genericDeliverable`), and history-reopen state (`reopenedRunStatus`, `reopenedFailedAgents`, `reopenedAgentNameById`).
- `handleWebSocketMessage` (and further callbacks such as `handleSelectChat`, `handleSwitchToLiveRun`, `handleRevisionLaunched`, `handleSelectWorkflowRun`, `handleNewChat`, `handleDeleteChat`, `handleLogout`) — the dispatch/handler layer that routes incoming stream frames and user actions into the state above.
- `phaseToConnectionStatus` — maps the SSE `RunConnectionPhase` onto the WS-era `ConnectionStatus` type so the header/reconnect UI is transport-agnostic.
- Composes several hooks (`useWorkflow`, `useRunChat`, `useTabDeepLink`, `useRunConnection`, `useRunStateStore`) and renders `DashboardLayout` with the assembled props.

## Why this shape
The file's own comments describe it as mid-migration from a legacy per-pipeline WebSocket transport to a generic SSE-based `RunConnectionProvider`, with structural (never workflow-name-keyed) dispatch throughout (SC-001) and several explicitly "additive, non-breaking" hooks layered on top of the original state — which accounts for its size and the density of state slots rather than a single clean design.
